sources.entry: CAJAL / PaperClaw - (Spain/International) Local AI for scientific paper generation with specialized 4B and 9B models. Features GGUF quantization, Ollama compatibility, and ranked #3 on scientific writing benchmarks. Open-source and designed for offline academic writing workflows.

summary.one_liner: CAJAL is a local, MIT-licensed Python tool that connects an Ollama/LLM backend to a scientific assistant for generating structured academic papers without sending prompts to a hosted API.
summary.what_it_does: CAJAL provides a CLI (cajal status, ask, chat, config) and a Python API (CAJAL.from_ollama) that send prompts to a locally running Ollama model. Its paper generator is described as producing 7-section papers (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Results, Discussion, Conclusion, References) and says it integrates arXiv and CrossRef for references. It also describes a "Tribunal" feature where several LLM judges score a paper on quality dimensions. The package includes a local OpenAI-compatible server extra and Ollama/Transformers/GGUF bridges in core.py. The README lists many integration kits (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, LlamaIndex, VS Code, Jupyter, Docker, etc.) as files in an integrations/ folder, and a large part of the repo is P2PCLAW ecosystem material, including a training dataset description.
use_cases: ask a local Ollama model research questions
scoring draft papers with multiple LLM judges
adding a scientific writing assistant to LangChain or CrewAI pipelines
drafting papers in Jupyter or Quarto notebooks
how_to_run: python -m pip install "cajal[server] @ git+ (URL truncated in README; install directly from the repository)
Install Ollama (macOS: brew install ollama; Linux: curl install script as shown in README)
cajal ask "What are the main challenges in decentralized AI governance?"
notable: Runs entirely on local hardware through Ollama; README states no API keys and no data leaves the machine
Integrates arXiv and CrossRef lookups for references
Multi-judge 'Tribunal' scoring of generated papers on 10 quality dimensions
Large catalogue of integration kits (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, VS Code, Jupyter, Docker, Chrome extension)
Repo includes a P2PCLAW training dataset description (751 papers, 7,140 records)
caveats: The README's install command is truncated, so the exact git URL is unclear from the text provided
The PyPI name 'cajal' belongs to an unrelated project; legacy cajal_p2pclaw code is not the installable package and is not covered by smoke tests
Requires Python 3.10+, Git, and a running Ollama with a compatible model

The listed claims in the external directory entry (specialized 4B/9B models, ranked #3 on benchmarks) are not substantiated in the README; the README mentions a cajal-4b model name only in the API example
